articles.title: Trump Hails Indian-Origin Astronaut Anil Menon as 'Great Patriot' During ISS Call
articles.excerpt: President calls Menon, Jessica Meir, and Jack Hathaway 'brave people' and invites them to the Oval Office; announces new US Space Academy.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-American astronaut from an immigrant family receives presidential recognition, embodying the diaspora's contributions to America's most ambitious scientific endeavors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Americans Back Democrats by 3-to-1 Margin Ahead of 2026 Midterms, New Survey Finds
articles.excerpt: The 2026 Asian American Voter Survey shows 66% of Indian Americans support Democratic congressional candidates, with 74% viewing Trump unfavorably.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American voters are poised to play an outsized role in the 2026 midterms, with high enthusiasm and strong Democratic preference driven partly by concerns over anti-Indian rhetoric and immigration policies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 51 Indian Nationals Killed Fighting for Russia as Death Toll Nearly Doubles in a Year
articles.excerpt: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri confirms 227 Indians recruited into Russian armed forces, 139 discharged; families still await remains and compensation.
articles.image_caption: India has confirmed that 51 nationals recruited into the Russian armed forces have died, nearly double the toll reported to Parliament in December 2024.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals recruited abroad under false pretenses have been killed in a foreign war, raising urgent questions about protections for Indians seeking employment overseas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sabyasachi Opens Lavish 26,000 Sq Ft Delhi Flagship With Met Jewellery Debut
articles.excerpt: India’s biggest luxury fashion store features a Kolkata-inspired design with 120 chandeliers and a Byzantine jewellery collection created with New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art.
articles.image_caption: Fashion designer Sabyasachi Mukherjee, who has opened a 26,000 sq ft flagship store at The Citadel in New Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: Sabyasachi draws 40% of revenue from the US with strong NRI demand, and the Met collaboration positions Indian craft as a global luxury force for diaspora consumers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anti-Corruption Icon Anna Hazare Hospitalised in Mumbai With Viral Infection
articles.excerpt: The veteran social activist was admitted to Bombay Hospital after severe dehydration and a viral infection, with doctors monitoring his condition closely.
articles.image_caption: Anti-corruption activist Anna Hazare, who was admitted to Bombay Hospital in Mumbai with a viral infection and severe dehydration.
articles.nri_angle: Hazare's anti-corruption movement mobilised millions of Indians worldwide, and his health remains closely followed by the diaspora community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The ISRO Chief Who Led India to Mars and Never Stopped Dancing Kathakali
articles.excerpt: Dr. K. Radhakrishnan steered Mangalyaan to Mars on India's first attempt while maintaining a parallel life as a Kathakali performer and Carnatic vocalist.
articles.image_caption: Dr. K. Radhakrishnan, former ISRO Chairman who led India's Mars Orbiter Mission. He is also a trained Kathakali performer and Carnatic vocalist.
articles.nri_angle: Radhakrishnan's story challenges the arts-vs-STEM binary familiar to diaspora families, showing a life where both passions thrived.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: RSS Chief Bhagwat Addresses Thousands at Madison Square Garden Amid Protests and Sanctions Calls
articles.excerpt: Mohan Bhagwat delivered a keynote on "universal oneness" to 6,000 attendees from 39 states and 29 countries as demonstrators rallied outside and U.S. religious freedom commissioners urged sanctions against the RSS.
articles.image_caption: RSS Sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat, who addressed roughly 6,000 attendees at Madison Square Garden on August 29 as part of the organization's centenary-year international tour.
articles.nri_angle: The event at Madison Square Garden brought together 6,000 members of the Indian diaspora from 39 U.S. states and 29 countries, highlighting deep divisions within the community over the RSS and Hindu nationalism.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Who Is Anima Anandkumar? The Mysore-Born Scientist Who Turned Down a Bezos-Backed Fortune — and Is Building AI That Understands Physics, Not Words
articles.image_caption: Anima Anandkumar speaking at the AAAS Annual Meeting in 2026. The Caltech professor was named a TIME100 AI Innovator days after launching her physics-focused AI startup, Accelerated Understanding.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How IIT Kanpur Graduate Satish Kumar Kaura Built Samtel Into a Rs 1,200-Crore Electronics Empire
articles.excerpt: From manufacturing TV picture tubes in a Ghaziabad factory to supplying cockpit displays for fighter jets worldwide, Padma Shri awardee Satish Kumar Kaura's five-decade journey with the Samtel Group traces the arc of Indian manufacturing ambition.
articles.nri_angle: IIT Kanpur graduate who studied and worked in North America before returning to India to build a manufacturing empire, representing the reverse brain drain that has strengthened India's technology sector
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Boy, 7, Scores Grade 8 in UK Maths GCSE Exam Meant for 16-Year-Olds
articles.excerpt: Jivyan Dhruva from west London scored 196 out of 240 on the maths GCSE, a qualification typically taken at age 16, and is already preparing for A-levels in maths and further maths.
articles.nri_angle: Seven-year-old Indian-origin boy Jivyan Dhruva continues a tradition of academic excellence among Indian diaspora families in the UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Army Pilots Execute Daring Helicopter Rescue at 18,600 Feet Near Nun Kun
articles.excerpt: Army Aviation crew evacuated a casualty from a steep Ladakh slope with no landing space, balancing the helicopter on one skid in fading daylight.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Army Aviation helicopter. Army pilots evacuated a casualty from 18,600 feet near the Nun Kun massif in Ladakh, operating at the edge of helicopter flight capability.
articles.nri_angle: The high-altitude rescue showcases Indian Army Aviation's operational capability in extreme Himalayan terrain, a source of pride for the global Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eight Indian-Origin US Nationals Missing Near Nepal-China Border as Families Plead for Help
articles.excerpt: Group of pilgrims from Telangana and Karnataka lost contact at Rasuwagadhi crossing on August 26, part of wider disaster leaving hundreds of foreign tourists unaccounted for.
articles.image_caption: An aerial view shows houses buried in sludge following the catastrophic flooding near the Nepal-China border. Hundreds of foreign tourists, including at least 90 Americans, remain unaccounted for after the disaster.
articles.nri_angle: Eight Indian-origin US citizens from Telangana and Karnataka are among the missing in the Nepal border floods, highlighting the deep ties between the diaspora and religious pilgrimage to Mount Kailash.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chouhan Assures Punjab Farmers India Won't Sign Trade Deal Harming Agriculture
articles.excerpt: At a BJP rally during Punjab's Rakhar Punia fair, the agriculture minister said no trade agreement would be signed that harms Indian farmers, while positioning the party for the 2027 state elections.
articles.image_caption: Indian Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. He assured Punjab farmers that India will not sign any trade deal that harms the agricultural sector.
articles.nri_angle: India's trade negotiations with the US directly affect agricultural exports and pricing, a key concern for diaspora members with family ties to farming communities in Punjab.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Public Services CEO Lax Gopisetty Unreachable After Nepal Floods as Death Toll Hits 579
articles.excerpt: The IT executive was visiting Nepal in a personal capacity when flash floods triggered by a glacier collapse killed hundreds and left nearly 2,000 missing, including 320 Indians
articles.image_caption: Infosys headquarters. The company's Public Services unit CEO Lax Gopisetty remains unreachable following the devastating floods in Nepal.
articles.nri_angle: Infosys Public Services CEO Lax Gopisetty, an Indian-origin tech executive, is among 320 Indians still uncontactable in Nepal. The disaster has directly impacted Indian pilgrims, tourists, and the broader NRI community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jan Dhan Yojana Turns 12 With 59 Crore Accounts and Rs 3.17 Lakh Crore in Deposits
articles.excerpt: The world's largest financial inclusion scheme has brought 89% of Indian adults into the banking system, with 56% of accounts held by women
articles.image_caption: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, India's flagship financial inclusion program, has reached 59 crore accounts with Rs 3.17 lakh crore in deposits as it turns 12.
articles.nri_angle: Jan Dhan accounts enable NRIs to send remittances directly to family members in rural India who previously lacked formal banking access, while the JAM trinity ensures welfare benefits reach intended recipients.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Tourist Praises Mumbai Locals After Free Treatment at Government Hospital
articles.excerpt: An American visitor who twisted his ankle in Mumbai was helped by locals and received free X-ray and treatment at a government hospital, drawing sharp comparisons with US healthcare costs.
articles.nri_angle: The viral video highlights the stark cost gap between Indian public healthcare and the US system, a reality familiar to many NRIs who navigate both.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Former Optum Director Sentenced to Three Years in $950,000 Fraud Scheme
articles.excerpt: Karan Gupta, 48, created a no-show job for a friend and pocketed kickbacks from his six-figure salary over three years, federal prosecutors said.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian American healthcare executive's conviction highlights fraud accountability among diaspora professionals in corporate America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and US Hold High-Level Nuclear Talks in Washington as IAEA Launches Maritime Reactor Initiative
articles.excerpt: Atomic Energy Commission Chairman Ajit Kumar Mohanty met US Energy Secretary Chris Wright to discuss bilateral civil nuclear cooperation, as India joined 27 nations in launching the IAEA's ATLAS initiative for nuclear-powered ships.
articles.nri_angle: Deepening US-India nuclear ties create opportunities for Indian-American professionals and companies in the growing nuclear sector, while ATLAS initiative could reshape global maritime energy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Australia Sends Aid as Indian-Origin Australians Among 39 Missing in Nepal Floods
articles.excerpt: Many of the missing Australians are Indian-origin pilgrims headed to Mount Kailash when the catastrophic flood struck the Nepal-Tibet border.
articles.image_caption: Floodwaters in Nepal. Australian authorities are assisting as Indian-origin Australians are among 39 people still missing in the devastation.
articles.nri_angle: At least 15 of the 39 missing Australians are Indian-Australians on a Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage. Indian-origin communities across Australia are holding vigils. Isha Foundation reports 77 pilgrims and 3 staff missing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Canada Launch Economic Dialogue, Signal Readiness for Investment Treaty Talks
articles.excerpt: Finance Ministers Nirmala Sitharaman and François-Philippe Champagne concluded the inaugural India-Canada Economic and Financial Dialogue in Toronto, setting an aspiration to expand bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion by 2030.
articles.nri_angle: UPI integration in Canada could lower remittance costs for 1.8 million Indian-origin Canadians; investment treaty and CEPA would strengthen economic ties for diaspora entrepreneurs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Lead UK Visa, Settlement, and Citizenship Numbers Across All Major Routes
articles.excerpt: Official UK government data shows Indian nationals account for nearly one in five visas issued, top the list for work-based settlement, and rank first for British citizenship grants among non-EU nationalities.
articles.nri_angle: Indians dominate nearly every legal immigration pathway to the UK, from work visas to citizenship, reflecting the diaspora's deep integration into British professional and economic life.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: PSU Employee Earning ₹23 Lakh Reveals Why Government Jobs Still Beat MNC Offers
articles.excerpt: A public sector employee's viral social media post detailing free housing, fuel, and electricity — with monthly expenses under ₹15,000 — has reignited the debate over whether PSU perks outweigh private sector salaries.
articles.image_caption: A public sector undertaking in India. An employee earning ₹23 lakh annually explains why government jobs continue to offer advantages over private sector MNC positions.
articles.nri_angle: The PSU-versus-private debate resonates strongly with NRIs weighing return-to-India career options, where take-home value often matters more than headline salary.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Student Applications to US Undergraduate Programs Drop 15% Amid Visa Crackdown
articles.excerpt: A Common App report shows Indian applicants fell sharply in 2025-26 as tighter immigration rules, a proposed $100,000 OPT fee, and four-year visa caps push families toward alternative destinations.
articles.image_caption: Students walk across a U.S. university campus. Indian student applications to American undergraduate programs have dropped 15 percent amid tighter visa enforcement.
articles.nri_angle: Directly impacts Indian families considering US undergraduate education for their children — covers application declines, visa policy changes, OPT fee proposals, and the shift toward alternative destinations
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kangana Ranaut Fires Back at Baba Ramdev Over 'Generation Gutter' Criticism
articles.excerpt: BJP MP accuses yoga guru of crossing 'every boundary of decency' as their war of words intensifies over her controversial remarks about Gen Z protesters.
articles.image_caption: Kangana Ranaut at a public event. The actor and BJP MP hit back at yoga guru Baba Ramdev after he criticised her generation as morally decadent.
articles.nri_angle: Both Kangana Ranaut and Baba Ramdev are widely recognized figures across the Indian diaspora; the generational values debate has resonated on NRI social media
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
